notes: πνεύματος ἁγίου is anarthrous, so the supplied 'the' of 'the Holy Spirit' belongs to the noun and not to the adjective (rule 58), discontinuously under rule 15.

τοῦ δοθέντος is the second attributive article standing after an expressed head noun, so the relativizer 'which' and the copula are the participle's helpers and the article realizes nothing (rules 23 and 31). Rule 31's postposed-article clause reaches verbless modifiers; here a participle carries the clause.
καταισχύνει → 'putteth ... to shame' heads on 'shame', the word glossing the αἰσχύν- root (rules 17 and 91).
